thread.title: New Apple iPhone Names, Prices Remain A Mystery

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: New Apple iPhone Names, Prices Remain A Mystery
text:
News leaks likely have stolen much of the thunder from Apple 's ( AAPL ) annual fall product launch event, scheduled for next Wednesday. But there are still several big unknowns, including names and prices for the new iPhones to be unveiled.
X Media and analysts expect the tech giant to introduce three 12th-generation iPhones at the event, being held at the company's headquarters in Cupertino, Calif. They predict an updated version of the 5.8-inch OLED-screen iPhone X, a 6.5-inch OLED model and a 6.1-inch LCD-screen handset.
Most Apple watchers say this is an "S" year for the iPhone, signifying incremental updates to the handset lineup. Starting with its third-generation model in 2009, Apple added an "S" to the names of iPhones every other year. But Apple deviated last year when it jumped to the iPhone 8 from the prior year's iPhone 7. It also added the flagship iPhone X, which celebrated the 10th anniversary of the first iPhone.
The consensus among analysts and the tech press is that the company will call its new flagship model the iPhone XS. That's led to jokes on social media that it will be pronounced "excess" and that the abbreviation also stands for "extra small."

Please contact customer service CLOSE Those comments assume that Apple will retroactively change what the X means in the iPhone X. Its proper name is "ten," as in the Roman numeral, not "ex," although some consumers still call it the iPhone "ex."
The name of the larger-screen OLED iPhone reportedly is the iPhone XS Plus. Some reports say it could be the iPhone XS Max.
The big-screen LCD handset could be called the iPhone 9. But some have suggested it could be the iPhone XC, with the C standing for color because it supposedly will come in a range of case colors.
Uncertainty Around Prices For New iPhones Pricing for the new iPhones also is a subject of debate. Several analysts have raised their price estimates for the handsets. They suggest Apple will use higher prices to sustain its profit margins and mine its premium brand reputation.
Apple's current iPhone X is its most expensive model to date, starting at $999.
New iPhone pricing is the biggest unknown heading into the product launch event, Raymond James analyst Chris Caso said.
"With three phones launching this year — and the Plus version representing a new price point — there is more uncertainty than usual," he said in a note to clients Friday. "Ultimately, we think sales of the Plus model will be the most significant variable that will determine whether Apple will beat or miss estimates, due to the expected high price of that model."
He believes the company will keep pricing unchanged for the iPhone XS handset vs. the current iPhone X. Caso expects a charge of $149 more for the base version of the Plus model.
Price-Target Hikes For Apple Stock Elsewhere on Wall Street, Piper Jaffray analyst Michael Olson raised his price target on Apple stock to 250 from 218. He kept his overweight rating. Apple shares dipped 0.8% to 221.30 on the stock market today .
He thinks the new iPhones will drive higher-than-expected demand. Olson predicted that Apple will sell 223 million iPhones in fiscal 2019, which starts Sept. 30. That compares with the consensus estimate of 219 million units.
Morgan Stanley analyst Rod Hall raised his Apple stock price target to 240 from 200. But he kept his neutral rating on valuation.
Analysts also expect Apple to launch its fourth-generation smartwatch at the event. Rumors indicate the Apple Watch Series 4 will feature 15% larger displays and enhanced heart-rate detection. Other rumors for the event point to second-generation AirPods wireless earbuds, as well as new iPad tablets and Mac computers.
